title: SSH, SFTP and AI,
in one native app
hero.lead: SSHYard is a free, open-source SSH and SFTP client for macOS, Windows and Linux. Work in the terminal, move files and let an AI assistant run commands on the host, all in the same window.
hero.note: Free and open source · No account needed · macOS, Windows and Linux

demo.aria: Animated example: in SSHYard, the AI assistant finds why a server returns 502 and fixes it while the terminal stays open.
demo.user_q: Since the deploy, nginx returns 502. What happened?
demo.a1: php-fpm stopped after the deploy: its pool still listens on the PHP 8.2 socket, while nginx now expects php8.3-fpm.sock.
demo.a2: I pointed the pool at the 8.3 socket and restarted php-fpm. nginx answers 200 again.

ai.title: An assistant that works on the host, with you in control
ai.lead: The assistant sees the terminal context of its host and runs commands and edits files over the same SSH connection. You decide how much it may do on its own.

modes.label: Ask
modes.text: The assistant asks you before it runs a command or changes a file.

modes.label: Review
modes.text: A review model checks every action. Only its explicit approval lets an action run; anything else comes back to you.

modes.label: Full access
modes.text: Every action runs without asking. Turning it on takes a confirmation, and a warning stays visible while it is on.

card.full_bar: Full access — every action runs without asking

ai.providers_text: Connect any provider that speaks the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses or Anthropic Messages API, including models you host yourself. Terminal output and file contents go only to the provider you pick, and only after you agree for that host.
ai.agents_title: Let your local agents in, on your terms
ai.agents_text: With agent access on, AI agents on this computer can list hosts, open SSH connections and run commands through the open API, MCP or the SSHYard Skill. They sign in with a token; your saved passwords and keys stay inside SSHYard.
agents_points: One-click Skill setup for Claude Code and Codex
Every command lands in the AI audit log
A new token disconnects every agent at once

security.title: Your credentials stay on your device
security.lead: Passwords, keys and tokens are encrypted locally. When they travel, they travel sealed.

steps.title: System keychain
steps.text: Holds one random 256-bit master key for SSHYard, and nothing else.

steps.title: Encrypted local store
steps.text: Passwords, private keys, passphrases, snippets and API keys are encrypted with that key in a single local file.

steps.title: Sealed backups
steps.text: Backups are compressed and encrypted on your device with a key derived from your password, using Argon2id and XChaCha20-Poly1305.

steps.title: Your storage
steps.text: WebDAV, S3-compatible storage and GitHub Gists only ever receive sealed files. The backup password itself is never stored.

points: Agents get a token, never your saved credentials
No account to create
Open source under AGPL-3.0, so anyone can audit it

items.a: SSHYard is a free, open-source native desktop SSH and SFTP client for macOS, Windows and Linux. It combines tabbed and split terminals, an SFTP file manager, port forwarding and an AI assistant that can run commands on the host.
Yes. SSHYard is free to download and use, and it doesn't need an account. Its source code is on GitHub under the GNU AGPL-3.0 license.

items.q: Which systems does SSHYard run on?
items.a: macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs, Windows on x64 and Arm64, and Linux on x64 and Arm64 as a .deb package or a .tar.gz archive.

items.q: Is SSHYard built with Electron or a web view?
items.a: No. Its whole interface is drawn natively, without a web view or a bundled browser, which keeps the download at about {size}.

items.q: Where are my passwords and keys stored?
items.a: On your device, encrypted. The system keychain holds only a random master key, and passwords, private keys, passphrases and API keys are encrypted with it in a local file. Nothing leaves the device unless you make a backup, and backups are encrypted before they do.

items.q: How does the AI assistant work, and can I control it?
items.a: Each host has its own assistant that reads the terminal context, runs commands and edits files over the SSH connection. In Ask mode it waits for your approval, in Review mode a review model checks every action, and Full access has to be turned on explicitly. It uses the AI provider and API key you set up.

items.q: Can Claude Code or Codex use my SSH hosts?
items.a: Yes, once you turn on agent access. Local agents can then list hosts, connect and run commands through SSHYard's open API, MCP endpoint or Skill, and SSHYard installs the Skill for Claude Code and Codex in one click. Agents sign in with a token and never receive your saved credentials.

items.q: Does SSHYard support jump hosts, proxies and port forwarding?
items.a: Yes. A host can connect through several jump hosts and an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy, and you can set up local, remote and dynamic port forwards.

items.q: How do backup and restore work?
items.a: SSHYard compresses hosts, credentials, snippets and settings into one file and encrypts it with your backup password on your device. You can keep it locally or send it to WebDAV, S3-compatible storage or a private GitHub Gist, by hand or on a schedule, and restore it on another device with the same password.

items.q: Can I import my existing SSH config?
items.a: Yes. SSHYard imports hosts from your SSH config file, and you can also connect straight away by typing user@host:port.
English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese and Korean, in the app and on this website.
